title: How Stone Tools, Fire, and Language Paved the Highway to Artificial Intelligence
author: Deborah Barsky
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/1920px-
Acheulian_bifacial_tools_hand-axes_Wellcome_M0015373-680x516.jpg)

Acheulian bifacial tools (hand-axes) from Burnham Beeches, Bucks. Image
Source: This file comes from the Wellcome Collection, a website operated by
Wellcome Trust, a global charitable foundation based in the United Kingdom -
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Many people are overwhelmed by the fast-paced evolution of mass communication
in a world increasingly shaped by the internet and artificial intelligence
(AI). Yet ideas have not always circulated across the globe at lightning
speed.

Looking into deep time allows us to view our current mode of existence from a
broader perspective and to discern patterns of change that may offer insights
into our species’ possible trajectories in the future. We can begin by trying
to identify the conditions under which humans developed complex symbolic
communication, which is considered unique in the animal kingdom. Today, we
have succeeded in transposing incredibly complex digital languages, beyond the
grasp of the human mind, into computerized systems capable of processing,
storing, and sharing all kinds of information with the push of a button or a
click of a mouse.

Human [language is at the root of this
system](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BMXJAdnUwV-2BnQoyEg-2BN5TXz4Qt4ve775UEH0ojRLKXzFJgz0dp446QMYetvsYdk-2B-2B9DklhpsFda5SHg2Y5bsxAY9pbt-2Fw1CIQwjNqWtQXAMRsi-2Bt2M3FX4L5705al28fLQ-3D-3D4e6j_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rYpjaerB-2FnMRBgc8iAQFILA4yMeOkMj6bXO7A0hx-2FCoEDTGNmwGPaUxUXhObwEC-2FyDQBFvpWY4rhS6gaMf5pQLyDYiYRDxGpafbjYuKdc0hgHGK-2BaF-2Fdi8C3eP3H4AOvlq3wPn4we9J-2FTFWKsZI5gyRp5jE5mY-2BKk7EvtOZNjlVJmmmvSAtHiM8Ci0UlNC6uNsvTlszjr-2FgTD2oD-2Fv2Qchrg-3D-3D).
While hardly perceptible in the archeological record, hominin physiognomy
assessed from the fossil record allows us to observe that the capacity to
vocalize across a significant range dates back to a very early time period.
Physical features linked to resonance complexity and articular precision, like
the low positioning of the larynx, an enlarged pharyngeal cavity, and a
flexible tongue housed in an ample palate, were already part of the human
anatomy by the time  _Homo erectus_ emerged in Africa nearly 2 million years
ago.

Somatic harmonization, necessary for speech production, is ensured by the tiny
and crucial hyoid bone, a floating anchor for the muscles controlling the
tongue, throat, and voice box as they work together to regulate sounds emitted
during speech. Paleoanthropologists studying the position, geometry, and
internal structure of [Neanderthal
hyoids](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BA3jN6PDPe8G3zUypPF1SFz-2F9fFxD5I2on9viora-2FvuL-2FSnJf6EBp1Gq46usSUlJMw-3D-3DVxe6_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rYNWh9x36c3r1n7vlWVxL95Zc-2BRyAXNHQ5Syu2GwuZ63ExVifKkp15NZltkWKgtEoW7dRjrIWG2MybTKE3Kfc9oRNynnG41HxZjT9MytUa3CaDa7qX3By0-2BE2jctWk0mbjps2Yb07AilIgcPpSMs4-2F4xKkYrZ99sGDhTuRJxOpCfpquz1rkGESrJPaar3f7oED0LRyUn5iwe9WoMIflcVqCg-3D-3D)
discovered in archeological sites found them to be nearly identical to those
of anatomically modern humans, suggesting that they were already capable of
emitting a similarly sophisticated range of sounds. Evidence from Spain also
reveals that modern hyoid morphology was [present by at least 530,000 years
ago](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BPlKSySdpjp1E3wiUlwR00tblWlOprPxjCAEedf7MvwdJm5oMG2ZUcmIICwFO-2Bs7ew-3D-3DSXps_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rY1pqjpa-2FqXVE4lsKttnET6oMHNz6c-2Fo5dAAo4-2B3JZCJ8Yyo0eT1p1w0C-2BLtuvfRD-2B7sANOsraUSyd2D2e-2F-2BYJhDmAz5hIukKhdpdzmo1KIqHzBPE2KJWYMea1XIfr6n8-2F4h47N9UHoGmLyZAvClIkWxXwu2N5-2B-2B0X70WBHs3fDlxQ0BKPIdzyc8iulUdIyS1SnJckU-2BeuymyR6e9e1ytb1g-3D-3D),
indicating that it could be a derived characteristic shared by modern humans
and pre-Neandertals, which they inherited from their last common ancestor.

The ability to emit a wide range of vocalizations characteristic of modern
human language did not appear abruptly, but rather, was favored over millennia
by interrelated adaptive elections taking place under the evolutionary
orchestration of both natural selection  _and_ [techno
selection](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BOfNE-2Fr4d42hklKAzvg0qXTWH0ng0KzKp-2B7hXQGBk9P-2BtLzzSe3MtpnW5ZbbZJhzXURCBamfcUudn25E3EIT4U6-2B60hqChjOCRXHSMSwtYEKY3VJZU1me6alaS5CHVuxIk3Nu-2FW6Rfqx9VTTd-2BTVWHc-3DzCbj_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rY-2Bq4InnzcIzWKHsOdlXLXMnX6gEO4NoWeMOegSl-2Fm-2F1dvuwcj1eiJ2UXztIeeeWRgNvK0k1MeUqn8gx8ly8G7L1ZQj37r4vLopVsQ3pRFG8BlI6-2BVLBX4-2BWacSFK2Ul90YOoHWGvtSww-2BPGl8wHdFzxgDfWSFOPm22XwSQ83s9jDCqVnw9wbZo0POtAey3hba5nuL8yYdoXuLYegE-2B9-2Baag-3D-3D).
As early as around 7 million years ago, some early primates displayed several
craniofacial modifications believed to have evolved, at least in part, to
accommodate bipedal locomotion. These included features such as reduced
prognathism, more gracile jawbones with smaller teeth, and a restructured
skull base, all of which subsequently facilitated the anatomical tweaks
necessary to increase the human capacity to pronounce a wide range of sounds.

By the time hominins began systematically making stone tools some [2.6 million
years
ago](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BNWYIlb-2FAdE9Uw7QDquAfRSctwKWZDgpAXBDQ0cDRMiTi-2FYDdx0Op1rWFdouB9fPTZktoOL718SQ-2FYMx0up3cHg-3DsTmN_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rYVIlyI-2FP9Zun9CqpoqK34TCg2jlv86BaybEEPsBe-2BgCB2ZA10pMJ8AqAPNOsIdx19F2o5GvhvyLaLlYbTXXJV6Ri8KBVvdNlNMWLjyvYSDPJ28FU0-2BIy6jqhQQjkFKL4C-2BQHKiw-2BzWl7FLuBxZfR9m5RjGlDCgHHyrttERxFAJK-2FZ1ierITN1hRgVrnWRDhl1ARoeywUQ7GR-2B-2B7vvs5hZkQ-3D-3D),
a series of changes in the archeological record reflected the significance of
this adaptive strategy. Around [1.75 million years ago in
Africa](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BNGfFAG5mDrs8-2B9JU5Emg2cIlMuv98IyBS3LBxUDQTWLz1pU8AXXPuZOZImoeIRifQ-3D-3DtixD_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rYohX-2BZre0dU2ak4giv9ud9w2HRbMaNoXsxXjgdP9Q284AuFvx9QxMuEtKxfehPVbGbfBCpKeF0LhOsureF1XhHUV4XH59H57dsoYeMxKO10Ng80rxKGA2WnhhuzjmEo7xfK1eCM9d8T81kH9wlv9HL9qQ71kaoxbVj29TpjSy-2BGbM5ftVwdNfyfuOMld-2BroqsZaE9OPUXL14B3ZVbByWNzA-3D-3D),
these (Oldowan) assemblages were progressively replaced by Acheulian
industries comprising tools with wider technological and morphological
variability, including skillfully manufactured and (esthetically pleasing)
premeditated forms, [like spheres and symmetrical pointed tools called
handaxes](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BEs9rWttVey5EbjXnC9DFdEy6q85h5xluoO68x9AHoOSxKy-2Bhsx-2BinBrly2EF2GENF7J7Ba9wNslqdY8NfiHM-2B2L16AojgY0JKHA3aOhis-2Fvea79_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bdpph-2BJclWEAF1gWkBDsknMk9nkKNbJRiufa6AOjJ7cYK1tCwscqPaNQIYzLSs3lbZaL-2FMtnjoNuqKpWr8jp-2Bpfl4fE22RIfVDJM6a2WDajju-2BEZ3yQwNAZ8UQVFzYFMjkLttcwdn-2BWd1N-2BUMh4-2BfvqHYIBx6ca7n25SNxWkR1yrRsJpQCirila-2Bv8MqgfKxduOaHLCmEvgAib0UFO0s9ckGUaszOSr-2B8zbuPyhGN92aUofq-2Biknf0VbkeqVG1sG9eEJatcExBgIC3WX65DSB3tlIMFsiAqpBOVhwvyenKahyBNKdKfRbbwd2-2F6JV2I9zp6FDI7l2Lv6vAYtDyj-2BzwtvvfMuOn8jMA7-2Bjtb5WAIEeknwQ4zilWENGzLpIrr65N3Yi9fZAYS8L-2BHaIABAs7NaDXAU9Ww9Deb2M8yB5sfIVK12rJV0WDNDx4SPSmoN-2BdAaH8l525y6hGN-2B8N1iAhY0-2FqwOqLTgrDu-2FvF7M3VDFx2T-2Fuov-2BYzpn9qpMehbxg8UIPsKky-2BVgCwWk4itzeOYDuXUucK277JYp-2Fq0Dca1jbLFSoWvmBIsry8N0n-2B1rY95Mu1nTgjXN-2Fa9XyDKGEVAm-2BYNZtVDyQKhTFnT-2FcN-2FWmq7zeBuuPE5RWRlCcMr0OotAvjqBvmK3WopFKP8JpoucAmmK4rCUrlwuEbCtj-2BkpbX1zSNMo0PXuFnEESf5DiPp12Afxii03OYyofX4AWVa-2FIb1UexN3waWRaqVoxCw8Xw0EOMz9qOJuwmhBoZ7HFc4NqCLywPnXoQdgHKX0Tzw-3D-3D),
which required high degrees of dexterity to make.

Observing synapses activated during experimental tool replication has shown
that the [cognitive processes involved in passing on the skills necessary to
make such tools are linked to those activated by

I have proposed defining this phenomenon as a fractalization process, insofar
as each branch replicates the underlying evolutionary patterns, overcoming the
constraints of its ancestral source while retaining the full spectrum of human
cognitive expression. In this model (that is comparable to biological natural
selection), small variations or adjustments can lead to exponentially
magnified outcomes through recursive and effectively infinite cycles of
reproduction.

By the time our own species came on the scene more than 200,000 years ago,
culture had flourished into symbolic material expressions, inexorably linked
to the technological and social realities of past human lives. Fire, for
example, provided ample fodder for experimenting with the power of
transforming existing materials, enabling new capacities during the Neolithic
and Metal Ages, with successive discoveries, such as pottery and, eventually,
glass and metallurgy, transmuting and enabling new societal paradigms.

Following the shift from hunter-gatherer to production-based lifeways,
technological complexity split individual role-playing into distinct
occupations, sharpening perceptions about (imagined) interpersonal “value”
within social settings. As populations swelled and collective living
arrangements expanded, these systems became structured around complex symbolic
interactions, material cultures, territorial identities, and hierarchies
constructed to sustain group cohesion. Importantly, social organization came
to rely upon artificially constructed (symbolic) notions that led regionally
assembled groups to contrast their ideas of communal belonging (identity) with
those existing in neighboring territories. As competition for land and
resources increased, these contrasting symbolic realities became a
justification for (sometimes violent) interpopulation conflicts.

Communication networks grew increasingly complex alongside expanding
production and territorial markets, accelerating the spread of cultural and
material exchanges. Protohistoric societies developed early writing systems
based on symbolic signs used as mnemonic strategies to represent ideas and
objects. Emerging independently in regions such as Mesopotamia, Egypt, Central
America, and China, these systems gradually evolved from pictorial symbols
into stylized phonetic and logographic writing largely detached from their
original visual meanings.

Throughout human experience, learning has been central to survival, with
scientific and behavioral complexification acting as a driving force to
develop sophisticated new ways to educate, demonstrate, and train each
successive generation to become effective agents of our seemingly unstoppable
technological proficiency. Presently, ideas move instantaneously across space
and time through global communication networks. Digital platforms make
information accessible worldwide, shrinking distances and connecting
populations, while promoting mass media and consumer culture. Often shaped by
corporate interests that influence production, consumption, and resource
distribution in a world driven by digital images and symbolic messaging,
global connectivity has become the force shaping human thought and social
organization.
